chunks: Whenever one of you drinks water, and says 'In the Name of God,' then drinks, then pauses and says 'Praise be to God,' then drinks and says 'In the Name of God,' then pauses and says 'Praise be to God,' then drinks and says 'In the Name of God,' then pauses and says 'Praise be to God' — that water glorifies God on his behalf for as long as it remains in his belly, until it exits.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: Alhamdulillah — 'Praise be to God'; the formula of gratitude said at the pause in drinking
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: Bismillah — 'In the Name of God'; the basmala invocation that sanctifies actions
key_terms.سَبَّحَ: Sabbaha — to glorify God (tasbih); the verb indicating ongoing cosmic praise
key_terms.قَطَعَهُ: Qata'ahu — 'cut/interrupted it'; the act of pausing between sips

ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually when a Muslim says Bismillah and Alhamdulillah while drinking water?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that when a believer punctuates their drinking of water with alternating invocations of 'Bismillah' at the start of each sip and 'Alhamdulillah' at each pause, the water itself enters a state of cosmic glorification of God on the drinker's behalf. This teaching reflects the Islamic concept that all created things inherently possess the capacity for tasbih (glorification of God), and that human conscious invocation activates and aligns with this natural cosmic praise. The hadith was transmitted through a chain that includes a rare female narrator, a daughter of Umar ibn Yazid, reflecting the broad transmission networks of the early Shia community.
